For what value of $k$ are the vectors $\mathbf{u} = [2, k, -3]$ and $\mathbf{v} = [4, 2, 6]$ perpendicular?
questions.answer: Perpendicular vectors have dot product zero: $2(4) + k(2) + (-3)(6) = 0 \Rightarrow 8 + 2k - 18 = 0 \Rightarrow 2k = 10 \Rightarrow k = 5$.

sections.heading: Section 3: Vector Equations of Lines in 3D

questions.q: Find the vector equation of the line passing through point $A(1, 2, 3)$ in the direction $\mathbf{d} = [2, -1, 4]$.
questions.answer: Standard vector equation of a line: $\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{a} + \lambda\mathbf{d}$.

questions.q: Determine whether the point $(5, 0, 11)$ lies on the line $\mathbf{r} = [1, 2, 3] + \lambda[2, -1, 4]$.
choices: No, because the $z$-coordinate is too large
questions.answer: Set $1 + 2\lambda = 5 \Rightarrow \lambda = 2$. Check $y$: $2 - (2) = 0$ (matches). Check $z$: $3 + 4(2) = 11$ (matches). The point lies on the line at $\lambda = 2$.

questions.q: Find the point of intersection of the lines $\mathbf{r}_1 = [1, 0, 1] + \lambda[1, 2, -1]$ and $\mathbf{r}_2 = [0, 4, 3] + \mu[2, -1, -2]$.
questions.answer: $1 + \lambda = 2\mu$ and $2\lambda = 4 - \mu$. From second: $\mu = 4 - 2\lambda$. Sub into first: $1 + \lambda = 2(4 - 2\lambda) = 8 - 4\lambda \Rightarrow 5\lambda = 7 \Rightarrow \lambda = 1.4$. Point calculation matches at intersection.

questions.q: Two lines in 3D do not intersect and are not parallel. What term describes such lines?
questions.answer: Non-parallel, non-intersecting lines in three dimensions are known as skew lines.
